payload.title: checkout() crashes for customers with no saved address
payload.markdown:
# Postmortem: checkout() crashes for customers with no saved address

## Summary
Brand-new customers who had never saved an address got a 500 at checkout because OrderService.checkout dereferenced a missing default address.

## Impact
Every first-time customer without a saved address could not place an order; they saw a generic error page instead of a prompt to add an address.

## Root cause
checkout() fell back to `user.addresses[user.defaultLabel]`. For users with no addresses that is undefined, and reading `address.country` threw a TypeError, bypassing the documented CheckoutError path.

## Evidence
- Logs show TypeError reading 'country' only for new accounts (u_1841, u_1842)
- Reproduction test 'checkout without a saved address throws CheckoutError' failed with a TypeError before the fix

## Fix
Throw CheckoutError('no shipping address on file') when no address is available. The first attempt (optional chaining only) was rejected by the tests.

## How it was verified
The reproduction test now passes and the explicit-address path still works.

- Reproduction test `tests/fixsi/checkout-without-address.test.js` failed before the fix and passes after it.
- Full suite: 32 passed, 0 failed (baseline: 30 passed). Pre-existing tests were not modified.
- Fix attempts: 2.

## Prevention
- Add tests for every documented error in public doc comments
- Map domain errors (CheckoutError) to 4xx responses in the web layer

---
